Framework Architecture

Pi-Index filters noise and yields quantitative results strictly aligned with Responsible Research Assessment (RRA) and CoARA (Coalition for Advancing Research Assessment) guidelines.

Intake & Identity Extraction & Heuristics Multi-LLM Panel PiDN Judge (adjudication) Ledger & Chain Outputs

End-to-end processing flow: intake and identity, extraction and deterministic scoring, the independent model panel, PiDN adjudication, and Proof-of-Research settlement on Sepolia.

Scoring Pipeline in Detail

Stage Reference

StageComponentWhat Happens
1Unified Intake & ZK-Identity RegistryORCID iD / W3C DID verification, local PDF, Unpaywall DOI resolution and OpenAlex discovery, ZK double-blind assignment.
2Extraction & Deterministic ScoringPyMuPDF layout-aware text extraction, MDAR adherence, RRID validation, reproducibility markers, empirical density.
3Independent Model PanelLlama, Mistral, Qwen and Gemini each assess the manuscript separately, alongside the local SciM structural analyser.
4PiDN AdjudicationWeighs the panel's independent verdicts into one judgement, and records the criteria weighting this paper implies — the input the PiDN forecast is built from. Cross-model evidence synthesis, inter-model agreement measurement, judgement-quality grading, adversarial logic integrity matrix.
5Proof-of-Research & TokenomicsBlock validation, zk-SNARK proof generation, criteria-weight recording, soulbound piQ minting on Sepolia.
6Dossiers, Cartography & ForecastingCoARA/DORA dossiers, AI defence rebuttal strategy, global map of science, PiDN LSTM epoch forecasting.

CoARA Compliance & Core Pillars

  • Diverse Research Outputs (C5 & C8): structurally evaluates open datasets, code repositories, and containerized executable environments.
  • Qualitative & Quantitative Balance (C1–C8): algorithms act as auditors, not replacements for peer review.
  • Transparency & Researcher Sovereignty: evaluation weights, logic states, and criteria scores are hashed and stored on Ethereum (Sepolia). Researchers retain sovereign ownership via DID/ORCID.

Framework Author: Ali Vafadar Yengejeh · Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca

HAL-OS live in your browser

A bare-metal ternary network that boots into the framebuffer: 32,000 neurons, no OS, no compiler, no font. The real boot image runs on an x86 emulator in this page — feed it images, a camera, your screen or any file, and watch it learn to reproduce them. Nothing you inject leaves your browser.

Compose quantum circuits on wires and inspect them: probabilities, state vector, Bloch spheres, density matrix and entanglement. A browser version of QuVI, the LabVIEW toolkit by Murtaza Vefadar (paper, MIT licence).
